A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Expected Return Symmetries, with matching authors, framework and experimental environments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original multi-agent experiments, including cross-play results in Section 4 and empirical tests of learned transformations in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results in Section 4, Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3, including coordination performance and transformation analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 revise the stated search space from action transpositions to tuples of local-action transpositions. The lever procedure now converts learned Q-values into Boltzmann policies. The overall symmetry-discovery and other-play pipeline remains; Boltzmann exploration for the other environments was already documented in v1 Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the three-lever game, cat/dog, Overcooked V2 and Hanabi. V2 identifies the Overcooked layout as Grounded Coordination Simple, but this clarifies previously unspecified coverage rather than establishing a changed test environment.

E2.justification: The specified comparator populations remain IQL self-play for cat/dog, IPPO self-play for Overcooked, and IPPO with and without environment-symmetry other-play for Hanabi. Removing the cat/dog numerical comparison changes result reporting without establishing a changed comparator roster.

E3.justification: Within the retained evaluation design, the lever reference-policy pool increases from 10 to 20 and uses Boltzmann temperature 1; cat/dog candidate OP policies increase from one to three; and Hanabi's reported inner-loop budget increases from 1.5e9 to 2.25e9 timesteps. The regularized transformation count changes from eight to eleven, resolving a discrepancy with Table 2. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: The Hanabi regularization/composition analysis, OP-optimality preservation check and conditional-action case study retain their evidence and findings. New Appendix C provides a theoretical explanation of an exploration failure, rather than a new empirical ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 changes the number of independent ER agents from ten to five, while Section 4.2 increases seeded candidate policies per agent from one to three. Explicit run and seed allocations therefore change, but no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: V2 removes the cat/dog mean cross-play scores of -2.11 ± 0.2 for IQL and 5.50 ± 0.02 for ER agents from Section 4.2, retaining a qualitative success statement. The Overcooked results, Hanabi Tables 1–2 and conditional-action findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 4 replaces return preservation over optimal epsilon-soft policies with preservation of the optimal Boltzmann-exploratory policy set. Appendix B revises the group proof and adds proofs of Boltzmann-exploration invariance under Dec-POMDP symmetries and the entropy-regularized local policy optimum. New Appendix C explains a failure of the earlier exploration assumption. These substantially revise the central mathematical foundation.

C1.justification: The introduction removes test-time symmetrization as a standalone contribution, although its policy-improvement claim and evidence remain in Section 4.4. The abstract, other headline contributions and conclusion retain their principal claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains how epsilon-greedy exploration permits exchanging the suboptimal reveal and bail actions, undermining grounded coordination, and why Boltzmann exploration distinguishes them. Section 3.2 qualifies the Q-learning connection as approximate because it is off-policy. Section 4.3 explicitly limits Overcooked evaluation to one layout.

D1.justification: Appendix A replaces a future code-release promise with notebook and repository links covering all four environments. V2 also documents the shared local-action transpositions used in Hanabi, names the Overcooked layout and explicitly states entropy regularization during transformation training. Most architecture, optimizer and hardware details were already present.

R1.justification: The cited-work roster and related-work discussion are unchanged. Positioning relative to other-play, off-belief learning, diversity methods and value-based abstractions remains the same.

P1.justification: V2 condenses portions of the introduction, background and experimental descriptions, adds acknowledgements, and reorganizes the proof appendix into subsections with a separate exploration-rationale appendix. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The three figure images and both tables retain their visual content and formats. Appendix layout changes place Table 2 with its discussion and separate Figure 3 from Algorithm 3, alongside revised equation spacing and page breaks.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the coherence of the central definition by addressing the harmful symmetries admitted by epsilon-soft exploration and adding supporting proofs in Appendices B–C. Code links and clearer implementation details also improve reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by removing the cat/dog numerical comparison and revising experimental settings without explaining their relationship to unchanged results, making the net improvement limited.
